narr: A late season cold front pushed southward across Central Alabama on July 9th. The air mass ahead of the front was very unstable with afternoon surface based CAPE of 4000-4500 J/kg and lifted indices around -7 Celsius. PWAT's were above two inches which also supported heavy rainfall and flash flooding.
ev: A line of very intense thunderstorms produced several inches of rain in a short period of time across southern Jefferson County. Many secondary roads along the I-65 corridor were flooded and impassable. Several vehicles were stranded in the flood waters.
Several roads flooded and impassable in the city of Lanett.
lsr: SEVERAL ROADWAYS WERE FLOODED IN AND AROUND LANNETT. RADAR ESTIMATES THAT SOME AREAS MAY HAVE RECEIVED UP TO 4 INCHES OF RAIN IN A SHORT PERIOD OF TIME.
FLOODING WAS OBSERVED AT HIGHWAY 31 AND HIGHWAY 150.
SEVERAL ROADS IN DOWNTOWN BIRMINGHAM, NEAR UAB, ARE FLOODED AND TEMPORARILY IMPASSABLE.
